title: Science & Nature
blurb: Space, the human body, animals and how the world works.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.fact: Two hydrogen atoms joined to one oxygen atom.

questions.q: About how many bones does an adult human have?
questions.fact: Babies are born with around 300, and many fuse together as they grow.

questions.q: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.fact: The Sun is about 150 million kilometres away.

questions.q: Which planet has the most famous set of rings?
questions.fact: Saturn's rings are made mostly of chunks of ice.

questions.q: What force keeps your feet on the ground?
questions.fact: On the Moon gravity is only about a sixth as strong.

questions.q: What is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.fact: Mitochondria turn food into energy the cell can use.

questions.q: Which gas makes up most of Earth's air?
questions.fact: Nitrogen is about 78% of the atmosphere, and oxygen about 21%.

questions.q: Which is the fastest animal on land?
questions.fact: A cheetah can reach about 60 mph in short bursts.

questions.q: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.fact: More than 1,300 Earths could fit inside Jupiter.

questions.q: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.fact: Insects have six legs, which is why spiders aren't insects.

questions.q: What do caterpillars grow up to become?
questions.fact: They change inside a chrysalis or a cocoon.

questions.q: At sea level, at what temperature does water boil in degrees Celsius?
questions.fact: 212 is the boiling point in Fahrenheit.

questions.q: Which organ pumps blood round the body?
questions.fact: A heart beats about 100,000 times a day.

questions.q: Which of these birds cannot fly?
questions.fact: Penguins use their wings like flippers to swim.

questions.q: What is the hardest substance in the human body?
questions.fact: Enamel is the hard white coating on your teeth.

questions.q: What kind of animal is a Komodo dragon?
questions.fact: It is the biggest lizard alive today and lives on a few Indonesian islands.

questions.q: How many planets are in our solar system?
questions.fact: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

questions.q: Which vitamin do we make when sunlight hits our skin?
questions.fact: Vitamin D helps keep bones strong.

questions.q: What do plants do to turn sunlight into food?
questions.fact: The word means 'putting together with light'.

questions.q: What is a group of lions called?
questions.fact: Prides are mostly related females and their cubs.

questions.q: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.fact: An adult's skin weighs around 4 kilograms.

questions.q: Roughly how fast does light travel?
questions.fact: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach us.

questions.q: Which blood cells carry oxygen round your body?
questions.fact: They get their colour from a protein called haemoglobin.

questions.q: What is the scientific study of the weather called?
questions.fact: It has nothing to do with meteors, despite the name!

questions.q: Which insect's cocoon is used to make silk?
questions.fact: One cocoon can be unwound into a thread about a kilometre long.

questions.q: Which is the only mammal that can truly fly?
questions.fact: Flying squirrels only glide, but bats really flap their wings.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for iron?
questions.fact: Fe comes from 'ferrum', the Latin word for iron.

questions.q: What is the smallest planet in our solar system?
questions.fact: Mercury is only a little bigger than our Moon.

questions.q: Which animal has the longest neck?
questions.fact: A giraffe's neck has just seven bones, the same number as ours.

questions.q: What do we call animals that eat only plants?
questions.fact: Cows, rabbits and elephants are all herbivores.
